summary: Martin Gusinde studied at the University of Vienna from around 1926 to 1928. He later held a post at the Catholic University of America from circa 1949 to 1957.

Martin Haug was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn under Rudolf von Roth, Theodor Benfey, and Heinrich Ewald. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1859–1866) and the University of Munich (1868).

Martin Heidegger was a philosopher who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1909–1916) under Heinrich Rickert and Edmund Husserl. He held academic posts at Freiburg (1915–1923, 1936–1940) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Freiburg and University of Marburg under Eva Tichy, Helmut Rix, and others. He held posts at Freiburg (~2000–2008) and the University of Jena (2013).

Martin Johannes Hammerich was an Indologist who studied at the University of Copenhagen and under August Wilhelm von Schlegel and Horace Hayman Wilson. He held posts at the University of Copenhagen (1841–1844) and as Principal of Borgerdydskolen i Christianshavn (1842).

Martin King Whyte is a Sinologist who studied at Cornell and Harvard. He held faculty posts at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University (1994–2000), and Harvard University, including acting director of the Fairbank Center.
Martin Kraatz is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied under doctoral supervisor Wilhelm Rau. In 1968, he succeeded Käthe Neumann.

Martin Lehnert, a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, completed his PhD at the University of Freiburg. He served as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich (attested 2016).

Martin Lowenthal is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu. He held posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Mills is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Edinburgh in 1997. He held posts at the University of Sussex (1997–2000) and the University of Aberdeen (Senior Lecturer 2000–2010; Chair 2024).
Martin Novosad was a Buddhist studies figure who studied as a disciple under Nyanatiloka Mahathera in 1938. In 1940, he served as the leader of Verdant Hermitage.

Martin Riesebrodt was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tübingen, Humboldt University, Heidelberg, and Munich. He was a professor at the University of Chicago (1990–2011) and the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies (2013).

Martin Schultze was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1855. He served as Director at Höhere Töchterschule in Cüstrin (1869–1877) and Rector at Theodor-Mommsen-Schule (1877–1885).

Martin Seeger is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Barend Jan Terwiel by 2004. He held a post at Hamburg (attested 2004) and served on the Pali Text Society Council (attested 2026).

Martin Straube is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Michael Hahn. His attested positions include posts at Göttingen Academy of Sciences, International Institute for Buddhist Studies, University of Bristol, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martin T. Adam, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He has served as an instructor at McGill University.

Martin Williams is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an MA at Keele University (1972–1979). He worked as an IT Adviser for Powys County Council (1989–2007) and Co-ordinator for the Religious Society of Friends (2011–2014).

Martin Willson was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Lambert Schmithausen and received her Dr.phil. from the University of Vienna. She served as Numata Professor at the University of Vienna (2021) and McGill University (2022).

Martina Palladino is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees at the University of Bologna and SOAS University of London. She held posts as Adjunct Professor at Bologna and as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2023).
